_readme: WORKED EXAMPLE — Walmart product page, hydration-state extraction.
Target: /ip/Dove-Body-Wash-Strawberry-Cookie-20oz/7843261295
Every path, selector and count below was READ OFF THE LIVE PAGE with real Chrome on
2026-09-02. The measurements in the notes are observed, not estimated.
WHY THIS PAGE IS THE INTERESTING ONE:
1. Its JSON-LD contains only WebPage and BreadcrumbList — NO Product. Everything a scraper
wants is in a 352,328-byte __NEXT_DATA__ blob instead. A recipe that only knew about
JSON-LD would come back empty from a page that is publishing all of its data.
2. The page renders six accordion sections — Product details, Specifications, Indications,
Directions, Ingredients, About the brand. They LOOK like six click-to-reveal problems.
All six are already in __NEXT_DATA__ under .idml, fully populated, before any click.
3. MEASURED, 2 consecutive loads with the full page scrolled to force lazy render:
__NEXT_DATA__  352,328 bytes both times; idml.specifications=10, indications=3,
directions=1, ingredients present, longDescription=455 chars — IDENTICAL.
DOM            9 .expand-collapse-header but only 2 .expand-collapse-content;
body innerText was 18,525 chars on run 1 and 32,183 on run 2;
the 'Product details' heading was present on one earlier load and
absent on these two.
Ingredients text in DOM: FALSE both runs. Directions text in DOM: FALSE both runs.
So the honest answer to 'what if JSON is not present, can HTML do it?' for THIS page is:
for Ingredients and Directions, NO — that text is never rendered into the DOM at all, at
any scroll position, expanded or not. The DOM fallback is genuinely degraded, not an
equivalent second route. Fields below carry html fallbacks ONLY where a fallback actually
exists; where it does not, the recipe says so instead of shipping a selector that will
always resolve empty. A candidate that cannot work is worse than no candidate: it burns a
page interaction and then reports 'empty' as though the site had changed.
4. THE AD TRAP. Under contentLayout.modules[1].configs.ad.adContentV2.data.products[0] the
page carries a SPONSORED COMPETITOR listing — 'St. Ives Soothing Body Wash', with its own
name, brand and priceInfo. An unanchored JSONPath '$..name' matches 203 nodes here and
returns the St. Ives string among its first few distinct results. Every path below is
anchored from the document root for that reason. See docs/recipe-json-extraction.md.
5. availabilityStatus was OUT_OF_STOCK at capture time while the page still showed a price.
Both are collected; neither is inferred from the other.
name: walmart-product
_sample_urls_note: One URL verified live. Per docs/recipe-operations.md D4.1 this stays draft until >= 3 same-type pages agree; verified_on below reports the truth (1).

variants.label: __NEXT_DATA__ present with the idml block — the normal case
No usable hydration state — degraded DOM-only collection

global_setup._comment: Bounded to 5s rather than 25s. On Zara, networkidle was measured never to settle at all; this page was not measured, so the wait is kept but capped -- it is on_error=continue, so the only thing a longer timeout buys is a longer wait before giving up.

brand.description: Brand name — the 'About the brand' section

item_id.description: Walmart US item id, from the /ip/ URL

available.description: Whether the item is purchasable right now

product_details._comment:
REQUESTED AS A LIST. Source is idml.longDescription, a JSON *string* containing
  • …
. html_select parses that string and pulls the bullets out — no regex over markup, no Lua.
product_details.description: The 'Product details' bullets, one entry per bullet

specifications._comment: REQUESTED AS A KEY->VALUE MAP. The source is an array of {name, value}; to_object turns it into the map the caller asked for. type.kind=object with empty properties means an OPEN map — the keys belong to the page, not to the schema, which is right for a spec sheet that differs per product category.
specifications.description: Specifications as a key -> value map, e.g. {"Scent": "Strawberry Cookie"}

indications.description: 'Indications' section, as a key -> value map

directions.description: 'Directions' section, as a key -> value map

ingredients.description: Full ingredients declaration, as a single string

inactive_ingredients.description: Inactive ingredients declaration, when the product separates them

field_groups._comment: One structured_data read serves this entire group. No clicks, no accordions, no scrolling.

name._comment: ANCHORED from the root. The competitor ad at contentLayout.modules[1]...products[0].name also has a 'name' key; only an anchored path is safe here.

name.note: DOM fallback genuinely exists for the title — unlike ingredients/directions.

brand.note: Observed value: 'Dove'. This is the 'About the brand' section's content.

item_id._comment: The URL is the most stable identifier on the page — it survives every redesign.

price.note: Observed 6.97 (number, not a string — no regex needed).

price._comment: priceString is '$6.97'. Different source, different cleanup — per-candidate transforms. With cross_source_agrees on the field, both are read and compared, which is what catches a selector drifting onto the sponsored ad's $5.22.

available._comment: Observed 'OUT_OF_STOCK' while a price was still displayed. map_lookup's null default keeps an unseen vocabulary honest instead of coercing it to false.

field_groups._comment: All six accordion sections, from the same single structured_data read. The DOM equivalent would be six clicks — and, as the readme records, would still not produce ingredients or directions, because that text is never rendered.

product_details._comment:
longDescription is a 455-char JSON string of HTML: '
  • Crumbl for Strawberry Crumb Cake cookies…now in a Body Wash
    • …'. html_select parses the string and returns the bullet texts as a list.
shortDescription is prose, not bullets — split on sentence ends so the caller still gets a list rather than one blob.

DOM fallback. [data-testid=product-description] does exist — but on 2 of 3 observed loads its body was empty and the 'Product details' heading was absent entirely. Kept at lowest priority and expected to be flaky, which is exactly what the fallback/suspect field_status is for.
product_details.note: container observed; bullet contents were NOT rendered on 2 of 3 loads

specifications._comment: 10 entries observed: Primary ingredient, Scent, Ingredient preference, Skin care key benefits, Skin care concern, Net content statement, Brand, Body wash & shower gel type, Features, Form. to_object turns [{name,value}] into the requested map.

specificationsV2 is the same data one level deeper, as groups of {displayName, attributeValue[]}. JMESPath flattens both levels and renames the keys in one expression; the simple dialect cannot express this, which is precisely when path_lang is worth opting into.

indications._comment: 3 entries observed: 'Stop Use Indications', 'Health Concern', 'Skin Care Concern'. NO DOM FALLBACK — this text was not present in document.body.innerText on either measured load.

directions._comment: 1 entry observed: {'Instructions': 'Squeeze body wash onto a wet pouf or washcloth and work into a rich, creamy lather.'}. Verified absent from the rendered DOM on both measured loads — there is deliberately no css candidate here.

ingredients._comment: Observed: 'Water (Aqua), Lauric Acid, Sodium Hydroxypropyl Starch Phosphate, …'. Also verified absent from the rendered DOM on both loads. No css candidate, for the same reason.
Some products populate activeIngredients instead; observed null on this one, hence verified_on 0. Kept because it costs nothing and covers a sibling product shape.
